{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that older age would be positively associated with a preference for helping colleagues over future-oriented work activities, and that this age-related difference would be eliminated under conditions of expanded time horizons.",
  "design": "mixed, with age as a continuous predictor and time horizon condition (unspecified, expanded, limited) as a between-subjects factor.",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "Experimental manipulation of occupational time horizons via written prompts: 'unspecified' (imagining unscheduled time), 'expanded' (imagining staying with the company considerably longer), and 'limited' (imagining a contract expiring soon).",
  "outcome_measure": "Forced-choice preference among three work activities: helping a colleague, working on a career-advancing project, or working on a project to lead the company in a new direction.",
  "population_and_setting": "Employed adults recruited via KnowledgePanel of GfK Research in the United States.",
  "sample_size_total": 555,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Recruited from a larger study about decisions and regret; no specific incentive details provided for this task.",
  "analysis_plan": "Logistic regression to test the association between age and the likelihood of choosing to help a colleague over future-oriented activities, including the interaction between age and experimental condition.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "The study used an adapted version of the Fredrickson and Carstensen (1990) social partner paradigm. Future-oriented options were collapsed for the primary analysis. Control variables included Future Time Perspective, education, and personality traits."
}
